provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Agriculture: soil and planting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to prepare a seed bed
The pupils should be able to sow seeds
Introduction:
Today we will learn about planting seeds. We have seen plants in our school compound.
Content:
A seed bed is a small piece of land where we plant seeds. We must clear the soil of stones and weeds. We make the soil soft with a hoe. We sow seeds by placing them in the soil. We cover the seeds with light soil. We water the seeds every day. Example: maize seeds in our school farm.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to prepare a small seed bed. They will sow bean seeds in the prepared bed.
Evaluation questions:
What is a seed bed?
How do we prepare a seed bed?
What do we do after sowing seeds?
Summary:
Preparing a seed bed and sowing seeds are important steps in planting.

topics.title: Agriculture: crops we eat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list root crops
The pupils should be able to sort crops into root, leaf and fruit
Introduction:
We eat different parts of plants. Some plants grow underground.
Content:
Root crops grow underground. Example: yam, carrot, cassava. Leaf crops have leaves we eat. Example: spinach, cabbage. Fruit crops have fruits we eat. Example: tomato, orange. We sort crops by where we eat them. In the market, we see these crops in different piles.
Class activity:
Pupils will bring pictures of different crops. They will sort them into root, leaf and fruit crops on a chart.
Evaluation questions:
Name one root crop.
Which part of spinach do we eat?
How do we sort crops?
Summary:
Crops are different parts of plants that we eat.

topics.title: Home economics: the home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name rooms in the home
The pupils should be able to list home care duties
Introduction:
Our homes have different rooms for different activities. We help keep our homes clean.
Content:
Rooms in the home: living room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom. The living room is for visitors. The kitchen is for cooking. The bedroom is for sleeping. The bathroom is for bathing. Home care duties: sweeping the floor, washing dishes, making the bed, keeping toys tidy.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw a simple house and label the rooms. They will write one home care duty for each room.
Evaluation questions:
Name three rooms in the home.
What do we do in the kitchen?
Name one home care duty.
Summary:
Our homes have different rooms and we have duties to keep them clean.

topics.title: Home economics: sewing basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to thread a needle
The pupils should be able to make a simple stitch
Introduction:
We can fix our clothes with sewing. We need a needle and thread to start.
Content:
Threading a needle: put the thread through the needle eye. Cut the thread with scissors. Make a knot at the end of the thread. Simple stitch: in and out, in and out. Pull the thread tight. Example: mending a small hole in a shirt.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice threading needles and making running stitches on a piece of cloth.
Evaluation questions:
How do we thread a needle?
What is the first step in making a stitch?
Why do we make a knot in the thread?
Summary:
Threading a needle and making simple stitches help us mend clothes.

topics.title: Agriculture: insects friends and foes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify helpful insects
The pupils should be able to identify harmful insects
Introduction:
Insects are small animals. Some insects help us, some harm our crops.
Content:
Helpful insects: bees help flowers grow. They make honey for us to eat. Ladybugs eat pests that harm plants. Harmful insects: locusts eat all our crops. Caterpillars eat leaves of plants. We can find insects in our school garden.
Class activity:
Pupils will go on an insect hunt around the school. They will draw and name the insects they find.
Evaluation questions:
Name one helpful insect.
What do locusts do to crops?
Where can we find insects?
Summary:
Some insects help us and our plants, while others harm them.

topics.title: Home economics: table manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to lay the table
The pupils should be able to demonstrate polite eating
Introduction:
When we eat with others, we must be polite. We set the table before eating.
Content:
Laying the table: place plates, spoons, cups and napkins. Forks go on the left. Knives and spoons go on the right. Eating politely: chew with your mouth closed. Do not talk with food in your mouth. Say thank you when served food.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice setting a table correctly. They will demonstrate polite eating using plastic plates and food.
Evaluation questions:
Where do we place the fork?
What should we do when eating?
Why is it good to say thank you?
Summary:
Good table manners show respect when we eat with others.

topics.title: Agriculture: harvest
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain harvest
The pupils should be able to name ways to store harvest
Introduction:
After plants grow, we harvest them to eat. We must store them well.
Content:
Harvest is when we pick ripe crops from the farm. Example: picking ripe maize from the stalk. We store harvest to keep it fresh. We can store in sacks, baskets or silos. We must keep harvest dry to prevent it from rotting. Example: yams are stored in cool, dry places.
Class activity:
Pupils will pretend to harvest crops from a paper farm. They will sort the harvested crops into different storage methods.
Evaluation questions:
What is harvest?
How do we store crops?
Why must harvest be kept dry?
Summary:
Harvest is when we collect ripe crops and store them properly.

topics.title: Home economics: mending
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sew on a button
The pupils should be able to patch a small hole
Introduction:
When clothes tear, we can mend them instead of throwing them away.
Content:
Sewing on a button: thread the needle, make a knot, push through the cloth, make a few stitches, tie the thread. Patching a hole: cut a small piece of cloth, sew it over the hole. Example: mending a torn shirt pocket.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice sewing buttons on a piece of cloth. They will also practice patching small holes on another piece.
Evaluation questions:
How do we sew on a button?
What do we use to patch a hole?
Why should we mend clothes?
Summary:
Mending clothes helps us use them longer and saves money.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship: class shop
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to buy and sell in play
The pupils should be able to count money correctly
Introduction:
We can learn about buying and selling in our classroom. We use money to pay for things.
Content:
In a shop, we buy things with money. We sell things to get money. We count money to know how much to pay. Example: buying a pencil for 5 naira. We can have a class shop with play items and fake money.
Class activity:
Pupils will set up a class shop. Some will be shop owners, others will be customers. They will buy and sell items using play money.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use to pay in a shop?
How do we count money?
What happens when we sell something?
Summary:
Buying and selling helps us learn about money and business.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show their sewing work
The pupils should be able to participate in market day
Introduction:
We have learned many skills. Today we will show what we can do.
Content:
We will show our sewing stitches and mended clothes. We will have a market day where we sell things we made. We will use the money skills we learned. Parents and other classes can come to see our work.
Class activity:
Pupils will display their sewing projects. They will set up stalls for market day and sell items to visitors.
Evaluation questions:
What will you show in the exhibition?
How do you set up a market stall?
What have you learned this term?
Summary:
We will show our skills and have fun at our market day exhibition.
